report:
**Conclusion: The claim is not supported by credible scientific evidence.** Major medical and scientific bodies have reviewed the research and found no causal link between induced abortion and breast cancer risk.

In 2003, the National Cancer Institute convened over 100 leading experts on pregnancy and breast cancer to review population-based, clinical, and animal studies, including on induced and spontaneous abortion (https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/abortion-miscarriage-risk). This comprehensive review found no credible evidence linking abortion to increased breast cancer risk.

The American Cancer Society's current position confirms this: "A 2018 report from the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine concluded that abortion does not impact a woman's risk for breast cancer," adding that "higher-quality studies have generally found no link between abortions and breast cancer risk" (https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html).

Susan G. Komen, a leading breast cancer research and advocacy organization, states plainly: "Research clearly shows abortion...is not linked to an increased risk of breast cancer," noting that both ACOG and NCI support this conclusion (https://www.komen.org/breast-cancer/facts-statistics/research-studies/topics/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk/).

While some older or lower-quality studies (often cited by advocacy groups opposed to abortion) reported an association, mainstream scientific consensus attributes these findings to methodological flaws, particularly recall bias in retrospective studies. As Wikipedia's summary notes, the "abortion–breast cancer hypothesis...is at odds with mainstream scientific opinion and is rejected by major medical professional organizations" despite continuing to be promoted in certain political and advocacy contexts (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion–breast_cancer_hypothesis).

**Bottom line:** The weight of high-quality, peer-reviewed evidence and consensus from NCI, ACS, ACOG, and the National Academies of Sciences does not support a link between abortion and breast cancer risk.
